citation: docs/architecture.md, durability: what can be written down is written down, and a live process cannot be. The rule that a saved region is a wish checked against the daemon follows from the same section - a daemon restart returns the pane tree and each pane's directory but not the processes, so a tab named here may or may not still exist.
why: Reopening is where a saved arrangement meets a session that moved on while the app was closed. Every region here is intent - the tab somebody chose, the width they dragged it to - and none of it is a claim that any of it still exists. So the decision worth pinning is which regions survive the check and where the keyboard lands, because both failure modes are silent: a region kept for a tab nobody holds renders as an empty square that never fills in, and a window that opens with focus nowhere ignores the first thing typed into it. The order is part of the answer too - regions are a list, and the list is the arrangement.

cases.name: everything is still there
cases.why: The ordinary reopen, and the one that has to keep order and widths exactly: a window that comes back with its regions shuffled or evened out is one somebody has to rearrange every morning.

cases.name: a tab that is gone takes its region with it
cases.why: The commonest way a saved arrangement is wrong: somebody closed that tab from another client, or its daemon came back from a reboot without it. Keeping the region would render a square that never fills in, which is indistinguishable from a daemon that has not finished describing itself.

cases.name: focus follows the region that had it
cases.why: Dropping a region ahead of the focused one shifts every place after it. Recorded as a place in the list rather than a name because ids do not survive the process, which is exactly what makes this shift possible to get wrong.

cases.name: the focused region is the one that went
cases.why: Focus has to land somewhere. A window that opens with the keyboard nowhere looks identical to one that opened correctly, right up until the first keystroke goes nowhere.

cases.name: a daemon that is not there takes all of its regions
cases.why: The devenv case: a laptop opened away from the network has no ssh daemon to attach, and every region showing it is a region with nothing behind it. The local ones are unaffected, which is the property that makes one unreachable machine cost one machine.

cases.name: nothing survives, and the window opens as a first launch does
cases.why: The state a laptop is in after a reboot took every daemon with it. Answering with no focus rather than a made-up one is what lets the caller tell this apart from a restore that worked, and open the way it would with no saved file at all.

cases.name: a saved arrangement that never had focus
cases.why: Reachable from a file written before anything took the keyboard. The first surviving region gets it, on the same reasoning as a focused region that went: somewhere beats nowhere.
